decisions.reason: The devore variants sit close to the core decoration collection and have stock and sampling invested in them, so management will likely keep them for reorder continuity despite the missing evidence after 2019.
The transparent burnout fabric is part of the publicly presented design-led collection, and any weak results can still be attributed to pandemic-related retail disruption.
This burnout fabric overlaps somewhat with B, but the samples and stock already invested and the firm's promise of reorder continuity favor keeping it.
The velour-like upholstery fabric builds on the firm's established upholstery line and is central to its offer, so dropping it would contradict the announced direction.
The flame-retardant inbetween fabric has required certification investment and serves steady contract demand, so it is a durable staple worth keeping.
The satin-sheen lining is a basic stock item that supports made-to-measure sewing and continuous reorders, with low carrying risk.
